title: Dashboard handshake & ownership sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational "handshake" process between product/feature owners and the observability team to reduce dashboard noise, clarify metric ownership, and establish a quarterly pruning cadence. Intended as a short sprint artifact (2 weeks) to align on ownership, retirement criteria, and a lightweight trace-retention plan for inference flows.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to dashboards and panels hosted in the shared observability workspace (inference, routing, kv-cache, paging).
- Includes alerts directly derived from these panels.
- Excludes third-party dashboards (customer-managed).
- Goal: reduce dashboard surface area by ~25% and lower average alert noise by the same amount for the quarter.

Hand-off model (the "Handshake"):
1) Feature owner prepares a 1-paragraph signal brief: what product behavior the metric surfaces, expected normal range, and three sample incidents where it would have been useful.
2) Observability reviews and assigns a steward (primary + secondary). Steward documents canonical metric name, canonical query, and a short justification.
3) Both parties agree to a 90-day trial: instrumented panel + provisional alert. After 90 days, steward runs a signal review (see Review checklist).
4) If signal passes (low false-positive rate AND demonstrable incident utility) -> promote to "stable" and assign to long-term owner. Otherwise -> retire or replace.

Metric def primer (sample entries - use this format to submit new signals):
- metric_id: inference.request.latency_p50_ms
- intent: surface median request latency for hosted-api route
- query_notes: quantile on frontend-proxy.histogram, exclude internal health-check routes
- normal_range: 25-120 ms (median depends on model family)
- cardinality: route, tenant_id, model_variant
- retention_tier: hot(30d)/warm(90d)/cold(365d)
- alert_proposal: p50 > 200ms sustained>5m (severity: high)
- owner: team/route-product-owner

Tracing span mapping (lightweight manual mapping for common inference flows):
- span: frontend.request.receive -> annotates request id, route, client region
- span: routing.policy.resolve -> chosen model_variant, fallback flag
- span: runtime.kvcache.lookup -> hit|miss, lookup_time_ms, kvcache_size_hint
- span: model.infer.token-gen -> tokens_generated, step_time_ms, kernel_variant
- span: response.serialize -> bytes_out, compress_flag
Notes: always include request-id as span tag. If a span includes PHI, mark in the mapping and apply redaction at instrumentation layer.

Dashboard visual lint rules (short checklist for any new panel):
- Single metric per visual: avoid mixing derived ratios and raw counters unless annotated.
- Explicit time scale: always show last 1h, 24h, 7d mini-tabs.
- Color semantics: green=ok, amber=degraded, red=critical. Use company palette.
- Axis annotations: always include units and a short tooltip description.
- Aggregation footnote: call out whether panel uses per-tenant weighting, global rollup, or sampled aggregates.

Pruning & retirement cadence:
- Weekly grooming in first 2 weeks of sprint 0: triage candidate panels flagged by ops or product.
- Quarterly prune: steward-run review for signals with <5 incidents or >30% false positives in last 90 days.
- Emergency prune: if a panel causes undue paging >3 false alerts in 24h, steward can unpublish and file a follow-up.
- Retirement steps: archive panel (mark name with archived/YYYYMMDD), migrate annotations to canonical metric doc, create short retro note.

Lightweight trace retention plan (cost-aware tiers):
- Tier A (hot): full spans retained 30 days, traces sampled 10% on high-traffic routes with request-id.
- Tier B (diagnostic): traces retained 90 days, sampled 1% globally; sampling bias for error traces and long-tail latency.
- Tier C (forensic): span summaries (name, duration, tags) retained 365 days; payloads/redacted fields discarded.
Notes: apply per-team and per-tenant quotas. Use trace TTL tags on ingest and enforce via retention worker.

Review checklist (steward-run, to be completed after 90d):
- Usage: panel viewed in last 30 days by >2 distinct users? (yes/no)
- Incidents: used in at least 2 triages / retros in 90d?
- Noise: false-positive rate < 30%?
- Cost: panel query cost < (budgeted qps * 2) over 90d?
- Actionability: does an owner have runbook steps linked?
Decision outcomes: promote | replace (with proposed replacement) | retire.

Operator quickcards (to include in dashboard header):
- "When this alert fires" -> immediate triage anchor (two bullets).
- "First check" -> how to confirm false positive quickly (two queries).
- "Mitigation" -> quick temporary mitigations (toggle feature, route to fallback).
- "Postmortem owner" -> who files follow-up.

Sprint tasks (2-week plan) - sample backlog items:
- Week 0: collect UIDs of panels flagged by oncall (Jayden) and product (Marina).
- Week 0: run query-cost audit for top-50 panels (Ravi).
- Week 1: steward assignment for top-25 noisy panels (Asha + team).
- Week 1: create canonical metric docs for 10 newly promoted signals (assign owners).
- Week 2: schedule dashboard snapshot & archive retired visuals.

Templates and artifacts to include on submission:
- Minimal signal brief (one paragraph) - required.
- Metric definition metadata (use primer format above) - required.
- Example incident trace id(s) - optional but preferred.
- Suggested alert text and severity - required for provisional alerts.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Enforce per-tenant trace quotas? (ops billing impact) -> action: subject to capacity study (ENGOBS-4187).
- Should we centralize retired-panel metadata in a single "archive index"? -> action: prototype index in a small sheet and evaluate queryability.
- Auto-suggest steward based on most-frequent viewer? -> action: experiment for Q3.

Appendix: short sample metric submission (copyable)
metric_id: routing.fallback_rate
intent: percent of requests that fall back to smaller models when primary model busy
query_notes: rate(requests where chosen_fallback=true) / rate(total_requests) per minute; exclude internal test-tenants
normal_range: <0.5% typical, bursts up to 2% during maintenance windows
cardinality: route, tenant_id
retention_tier: warm(90d)
alert_proposal: fallback_rate > 3% for 10m outside rolling-maintenance windows (severity: medium)
owner: platform-routing

Contact and next sync:
- Observability weekly sync: Tuesdays 11:00 PT
- Owners sync for this sprint: Thu 2025-06-19 09:30 PT
- Primary contact: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai)

End of doc."
